study_identification_part.si_4_title: Neurofind: using deep learning to make individualised inferences in brain-based disorders

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: HCP-YA, HCP-A, UK Biobank, and IXI were used for model development. AIBL, MCIC, and COBRE were used for exemplar applications.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Data for training the web-based normative models used in Neurofind consisted of four publicly available datasets of healthy controls, namely the Human Connectome Project [61, 62], the Human Connectome Project Aging [63], Biobank [64] and IXI... Exemplar applications were carried out in three clinical datasets: the Australian Imaging, Biomarkers and Lifestyle Study (AIBL), the MIND Clinical Imaging Consortium (MCIC) and the Center for Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE) dataset."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The first four datasets were used to train the normative models. The latter three were used to demonstrate the tool's application in Alzheimer's Disease (AIBL) and Schizophrenia (MCIC, COBRE).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Data for training the web-based normative models... consisted of four publicly available datasets... Exemplar applications were carried out in three clinical datasets..."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The model was trained on 3362 HCs. For the exemplar applications (testing), an additional 61 HCs (AIBL) and 111 HCs (MCIC+COBRE) were used.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The tool was trained on 3362 images of healthy controls... Table 1. Train set (N = 3362)... Table 2. Clinical datasets (N = 367)... HC (N = 61)... HC (N = 111)"
